transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

The 'Er03' code on AEG hobs is not a standard global error, but given that your pasta boiled over immediately before it happened, this is almost certainly a spillage issue. Liquid tracking under the glass or into the control panel can cause short circuits or sensor errors that trigger beeping and shutdowns. Please switch off the hob at the wall (isolate it) and leave it for at least 24 hours to dry out completely. Do not use it until it is bone dry. After drying, try turning it on again. If the error returns even when the surface is dry, or if you smell burning plastic, stop using it immediately and call an engineer, as this could indicate internal damage to the control board.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I wiped it dry and switched it off at the wall for about 5 minutes rather than 24 hours, and it's working again now. Is that ok, or do I still need to leave it for the full 24 hours?

Since the hob has reset and is working normally again after just 5 minutes, it suggests that only surface moisture caused a temporary short rather than deep-seated damage to the internal electronics. You can use your hob as normal now; just be sure to wipe up any future boil-overs immediately before they track under the glass or into the controls.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

reading.symptom: keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make AEG; model IKB64301FB; code ER03.
The fault they reported is: "keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

reading.symptom: error code and shutdown after pasta boiled over

plan: They asked: "Is that ok, or do I still need to leave it for the full 24 hours?" - answer that first.
The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.

facts.value: switched off at the wall for about 5 minutes: working again
